title: aggregate: PostgreSQL buckets a non-UTC timezone in the database (amend ADR-0053 D2; SQLite keeps DST zones in memory) — epic #33631 R6
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cztR1A2CZoxSZyuoGP

Filing gate: ④ child of epic #33631 (SQL performance; maintainer's direct word on the epic). Item R6 of the M0 ranked list (#33633): https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/33631#issuecomment-6889544281.

## Maintainer ruling (seat decision card, 2026-11-15T06:40Z)

「PG 在库里算，修订 ADR」: amend ADR-0053 Phase 2 D2 (UTC-only native date bucketing) so that **PostgreSQL** buckets a non-UTC `timezone` in the database (zone-aware `date_trunc(... AT TIME ZONE tz)`, DST-correct). SQLite has no tz database, so DST zones stay in memory there (a fixed-offset zone may be bucketed in SQL if the PR measures it safe). The ADR amendment follows the governed path (Tier H).

## Today

A non-UTC date bucket forces the in-memory aggregate (`engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` ~1323–1341): every row of the scoped set is fetched into the app.

## Measured (`analytics_month_tz`, 1M rows, 100k opportunities)

Zone-aware SQL bucket: PG 429 → 40 ms (11x); SQLite fixed-offset 198 → 71 ms.

## Rules

- Parity test: PG in-database buckets equal the in-memory buckets for a DST zone across a DST boundary (e.g. Europe/Berlin March/October) and for Asia/Taipei.
- Security never regresses: the read scope and tenant wall stay in the aggregate's WHERE.
- Driver capability decides; memory/Mongo keep today's path or refuse per the epic rules.

## Business reason

Most users are not in UTC (e.g. Taipei); every monthly/daily dashboard for them pays the in-memory path today.

## Reader

domain:server#5 area A4 (engine aggregate + driver-sql capability), next account; size M. Before/after on the M0 bench (PR #33662).

## Dedupe

Covered by the M0 inventory; no open card on non-UTC native bucketing.
